review_notes: Read the whole file and Holder.lean's integrable_of_bilin_of_bdd_left. I looked at the helper chain (simpleFunc, bound, ae-bound, general), the flip wrappers, and the smul/mul specializations. The flip, smul and mul wrappers are thin and I did not flag them. I flagged two repeated patterns: re-proving that the condExp of B f μ[g|m] is itself (twice, inside condExp_stronglyMeasurable_bilin_of_bound), and the AE-to-strongly-measurable representative reduction (duplicated in two theorems). I could not run Lean, so the proposed helpers are untested. The second is weaker because its repeated steps are short; the first is the stronger case. I did not check whether a finite-measure instance or a bare SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm) assumption is the better choice for the first helper.

findings.excerpt: Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable (g := (fun z : F × E ↦ B z.1 z.2)) (by fun_prop)
findings.problem: The proof shows twice that the conditional expectation of `B h μ[g|m]` equals `B h μ[g|m]` for a bounded m-strongly-measurable `h`. First `h = f` (lines 100-105, via `this`). Then `h = fs n` (lines 126-133, via `nth_rw 2 [condExp_of_stronglyMeasurable hm]`). Each time it rebuilds the same chain: measurability of `B h μ[g|m]` through `Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable ... (… .prodMk stronglyMeasurable_condExp)`, then `integrable_of_bilin_of_bdd_left c … integrable_condExp`, then `condExp_of_stronglyMeasurable`. The `nth_rw 2` call is also fragile.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a private lemma before `condExp_stronglyMeasurable_bilin_of_bound`:
`lemma condExp_bilin_condExp_of_bound [CompleteSpace E] (hm : m ≤ mΩ) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {f : Ω → F} {g : Ω → E} (hf : StronglyMeasurable[m] f) (c : ℝ) (hf_bound : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ‖f ω‖ ≤ c) : μ[fun ω ↦ B (f ω) (μ[g | m] ω) | m] = fun ω ↦ B (f ω) (μ[g | m] ω)`.
Proof: `condExp_of_stronglyMeasurable hm (Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable (g := fun z : F × E ↦ B z.1 z.2) (by fun_prop) (hf.prodMk stronglyMeasurable_condExp)) (B.integrable_of_bilin_of_bdd_left c (hf.mono hm).aestronglyMeasurable hf_bound integrable_condExp)`.
Then `this` at line 100 becomes `condExp_bilin_condExp_of_bound B hm hf c hf_bound`. The last bullet becomes `(condExp_stronglyMeasurable_simpleFunc_bilin B hm _ hg).trans (EventuallyEq.of_eq (condExp_bilin_condExp_of_bound B hm (fs n).stronglyMeasurable c (ae_of_all _ <| hfs_bound n)).symm)`. The same lemma could also supply the integrability facts at lines 113-115, which repeat the `integrable_of_bilin_of_bdd_left … integrable_condExp` pattern.
findings.benefit: The measurability, integrability and idempotence argument appears once with a named statement. The main proof no longer has the 8-line duplicate block or the positional `nth_rw 2`. Any later change, for example to the hypotheses of `condExp_of_stronglyMeasurable`, is made in one place.

findings.problem: Both theorems extend a strongly-measurable result to an a.e.-strongly-measurable `f` with the same three-step `calc`. Step 1 replaces `f` by `hf.mk f` inside the condExp via `condExp_congr_ae`. Step 2 applies the strongly-measurable theorem to `hf.mk f` and transfers its hypotheses along `hf.ae_eq_mk`. Step 3 replaces `hf.mk f` by `f` on the right-hand side. Steps 1 and 3 are copied almost verbatim, and `f` is rewritten along `hf.ae_eq_mk` four times in total.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a congruence lemma: `lemma condExp_bilin_congr_left_iff {f f' : Ω → F} {g : Ω → E} (h : f =ᵐ[μ] f') : (μ[fun ω ↦ B (f ω) (g ω) | m] =ᵐ[μ] fun ω ↦ B (f ω) (μ[g | m] ω)) ↔ (μ[fun ω ↦ B (f' ω) (g ω) | m] =ᵐ[μ] fun ω ↦ B (f' ω) (μ[g | m] ω))`.
Proof sketch: use `condExp_congr_ae` on the left sides and `filter_upwards [h]` plus `rw` on the right sides, then `EventuallyEq.congr` or `eventuallyEq_congr`.
Both theorems then become `(condExp_bilin_congr_left_iff B hf.ae_eq_mk).2 (<strongly measurable theorem for hf.mk f>)`. The first supplies the bound by `filter_upwards [hf_bound, hf.ae_eq_mk]`. The second supplies integrability by `(integrable_congr …).mp hfg`.
findings.benefit: The two proofs shrink to the one step that differs, namely which strongly measurable theorem is invoked and how its hypotheses are transferred. The ae-congruence bookkeeping is stated once, and a future variant, such as an a.e. version of the right-hand pull-out, can reuse it.
